title: DashboardProgressApi
description: Request and response shapes of the progress service (AGB-1067 section 4), under /api/v1/progress. Identity is taken from the token headers Kong forwards (x-user-id, x-profile-id, x-guardian-id), never from a body.

EventIntakeRequest.title: EventIntakeRequest
EventIntakeRequest.description: POST /events (student token) and POST /events/parent (parent token). At most BATCH_MAX = 50 events; more is BATCH_TOO_LARGE.

EventResult.title: EventResult
EventResult.description: Per-event outcome. `error` is present only when result is error (for example EVENT_INVALID). From 2.23.0 an error is one of EVENT_INVALID (permanent), EVENT_KIND_NOT_ALLOWED (permanent: a self learner sent a kind other than note), LINK_ERASED (permanent) or SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED (version skew: keep the event and retry after an app update). Unknown codes must be treated like SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED.

EventIntakeResponse.title: EventIntakeResponse
EventIntakeResponse.description: One result per event, in request order.

ChangesResponse.title: ChangesResponse
ChangesResponse.description: GET /students/{studentId}/changes?since={cursor}. An old cursor answers CURSOR_EXPIRED.

audience.description: Added in 2.23.0. Who can read this note, computed at read time. Documented values: `only-me` (a learner without a guardian) and `guardian` (a guarded learner: the guardian sees notes saved after the claim). A later release may add values, so readers must tolerate an unknown string; deliberately not a closed enum.

guardianVisible.description: Added in 2.23.0. True when the learner's guardian can read this note under the claim rule (a note written before the claim stays private). Computed at read time.

quoteOffset.description: Added in 2.23.0. Character offset of `quote` inside the block text, read back so the app can reopen at the pin. Absent when the note has none.

status.description: Added in 2.26.0 (what the server has always sent). The note thread state: `open` (no reply yet), `replied` (a guardian replied), `resolved`. Optional: a client must not require it.

statusKey.description: Added in 2.26.0. The i18n key of `status`, always `notes.status.<status>`.

tagKey.description: Added in 2.26.0. The i18n key of `tag`: the tag lower-cased, apostrophes dropped, other runs of non-alphanumerics as `_` (`Rough note` is `notes.tag.rough_note`, `I don't get this` is `notes.tag.i_dont_get_this`).

edited.description: Added in 2.26.0. True when the note has more than one version (`latestVersion` above 1).

updatedAt.description: Added in 2.26.0. When the note last changed (equals `createdAt` for a note never edited).

quoteOffset.description: Added in 2.23.0. Character offset of `quote` inside the block text (0 or more), so the pin survives a style or language switch and the editor can reopen at the exact place. Sent on `create` and `edit` only; the service ignores it on `delete`. Optional: a 2.22 event without it is unchanged. If the block is missing, the app falls to the nearest block with a notice.

EditNoteRequest.title: EditNoteRequest

quoteOffset.description: Added in 2.23.0. Character offset of `quote` inside the block text (0 or more), so the pin survives a style or language switch and the editor can reopen at the exact place. Sent on `create` and `edit` only; the service ignores it on `delete`. Optional: a 2.22 event without it is unchanged. If the block is missing, the app falls to the nearest block with a notice.

EditNoteRequest.description: PATCH /students/{id}/notes/{noteId}: makes a new version. DELETE has no body.

NoteListResponse.title: NoteListResponse
NoteListResponse.description: GET /students/{id}/notes and GET /learners/me/notes (filters: chapter, tag, and from 2.23.0 `cursor` and `limit`, see NoteListQuery). Newest first; no repeats or skips between pages.

cursor.description: Added in 2.23.0. The documented paging field: pass as `cursor` for the next (older) page; null or absent on the last page. The progress service returns both `cursor` and `nextCursor` with the same value; clients should read `cursor`. Absent means a 2.22 server (everything in one answer).

studentId.description: Added in 2.26.0 (what the server has always sent). The learner whose notes these are; an echo of the path id, or of the caller for `/learners/me`.

nextCursor.description: Added in 2.26.0. An alias of `cursor` that the progress service also sends (always the same value). Optional; clients should read `cursor`.

NoteReplyRequest.title: NoteReplyRequest
NoteReplyRequest.description: POST /students/{id}/notes/{noteId}/replies: text, a reaction, or both.

ReviewDoneResponse.title: ReviewDoneResponse
ReviewDoneResponse.description: Marks done and writes a review-done event.

CatchUpResponse.title: CatchUpResponse
CatchUpResponse.description: GET /guardians/me/catch-up: the three that matter most.

NoteSearchRequest.title: NoteSearchRequest
NoteSearchRequest.description: POST /learners/me/notes/search (2.23.0). A POST so that note-derived text never reaches a URL, Kong or access logs; there is no GET `q`. The service never logs this body. `q` is NFC-normalised and matched as a case-insensitive substring over `text` and `quote` of the caller's own notes.

createdFrom.description: Added in 2.27.0. Only notes created on or after this day (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, UTC day start 00:00:00.000Z). Optional. A real calendar date; an invalid date, or createdFrom after createdTo, is a 400 INVALID_PARAMETER. It only narrows the result: a guardian still sees only notes created after the claim.

createdTo.description: Added in 2.27.0. Only notes created on or before this day (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, UTC day end 23:59:59.999Z). Optional. Same rules as createdFrom.

NoteSearchResponse.title: NoteSearchResponse
NoteSearchResponse.description: Answer of POST /learners/me/notes/search (2.23.0): newest first; no repeats or skips between pages. A learner with no link row gets an empty list (200).

cursor.description: The documented paging field: pass as `cursor` for the next page; null or absent on the last page. The progress service returns both `cursor` and `nextCursor` with the same value; clients should read `cursor`.

studentId.description: Added in 2.26.0 (what the server has always sent). The learner whose notes these are; an echo of the path id, or of the caller for `/learners/me`.

nextCursor.description: Added in 2.26.0. An alias of `cursor` that the progress service also sends (always the same value). Optional; clients should read `cursor`.

NoteVersionsResponse.title: NoteVersionsResponse
NoteVersionsResponse.description: GET /learners/me/notes/{noteId}/versions and GET /students/{id}/notes/{noteId}/versions (2.23.0): the versions of one note, oldest first, replayed from its events. A deleted note is a tombstone and answers 404, never this shape.

LearnerRelation.title: LearnerRelation
LearnerRelation.description: How a learner's notes are held (2.23.0). `none`: nothing is recorded (no link, or after a rollback). `self`: an adult learner with their own consent and no guardian; notes are private. `guarded`: a child with a guardian; the guardian reads notes saved after the claim.

LearnerStatusResponse.title: LearnerStatusResponse
LearnerStatusResponse.description: GET /learners/me/status (2.23.0). With no link row at all the service answers 200 `{ relation: "none", recording: "off", guardianVisible: false, guardianSince: null }`.

recording.description: Whether the service accepts note events now. Documented values: `active` (accepted) and `off` (not accepted). A string so a newer server value never fails a strict client; treat anything but `active` as off.

guardianVisible.description: True when a guardian can read notes saved from now on.

guardianSince.description: The server sequence watermark of the claim: the guardian sees only notes created after it. A new value tells the app to show the one-time claim sheet before it flushes the outbox. 0 for a guarded profile with nothing older; null for `none` and `self`.

DeletedNote.title: DeletedNote
DeletedNote.description: A deleted note in an export (2.23.0): its id and deletion time only; the text and quote are redacted and never exported.

SelfExportNote.title: SelfExportNote
SelfExportNote.description: A live note in a learner's own export (2.23.0), with all its versions. No other person's id or name appears: guardian replies are not part of the self export.

quoteOffset.description: Added in 2.23.0. Character offset of `quote` inside the block text (0 or more), so the pin survives a style or language switch and the editor can reopen at the exact place. Sent on `create` and `edit` only; the service ignores it on `delete`. Optional: a 2.22 event without it is unchanged. If the block is missing, the app falls to the nearest block with a notice.

SelfExportResponse.title: SelfExportResponse
SelfExportResponse.description: POST /students/{id}/export when `id` is the caller's own id (2.23.0; self learners only: a guarded child cannot export their own notes, the guardian does). Restricted shape: the learner's own notes with versions, deleted notes as `{ id, deletedAt }`, no other person's id or name. With no link row the export is an empty document (`notes: []`). Own export stays open for a withdrawn or `none` link.

NoteListQuery.title: NoteListQuery
NoteListQuery.description: Query parameters of the notes list (2.23.0), shown as an object. There is no `q`: search is a POST (NoteSearchRequest), so note text never reaches a URL.

createdFrom.description: Added in 2.27.0. Only notes created on or after this day (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, UTC day start 00:00:00.000Z). Optional. A real calendar date; an invalid date, or createdFrom after createdTo, is a 400 INVALID_PARAMETER. It only narrows the result: a guardian still sees only notes created after the claim.

createdTo.description: Added in 2.27.0. Only notes created on or before this day (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, UTC day end 23:59:59.999Z). Optional. Same rules as createdFrom.

LearnerEraseRequest.title: LearnerEraseRequest
LearnerEraseRequest.description: POST /learners/me/learning-record/erase (2.23.0, adult token): permanent and terminal for the account. The body carries the single-use step-up ticket from step-up/complete; the answer is DataRequestResult. A missing, expired or used ticket is STEP_UP_REQUIRED.
